perf.summary: The per-round team rotation is an O(numTeams) array shift; the entire schedule can be generated by index arithmetic with no rotation buffer.
perf.currentCost: Each of `rounds` rounds does a backward copy loop shifting teams[1..numTeams-1], i.e. O(numTeams) memory moves per round => O(numTeams^2) total writes plus the match emission, and the rotation creates a serial dependency that Burst cannot vectorize.
perf.proposedChange: Replace the rotation with the standard circle method closed form: team 0 is fixed; for round r and slot i, the opponent indices are computed as (r + i) mod (numTeams-1) and (r - i mod (numTeams-1)) with the fixed slot handled separately, writing matches directly. This removes the teams[] buffer and the shift loop entirely.
perf.rationale: Turns O(numTeams^2) data movement into O(numTeams^2) pure index math with zero memory shuffling and no loop-carried dependency on the teams array, which Burst vectorizes/pipelines far better and drops a stackalloc.
perf.risk: The closed-form must reproduce the EXACT same pairing and the same t1/t2 ordering and the same -1 bye encoding as the current rotation, otherwise observable output (schedule[] contents/order) changes. This requires careful derivation and a parity check against the current algorithm before adopting; if exact-order parity cannot be guaranteed, keep the rotation. Flagged as a candidate, not a drop-in.

perf.summary: isOdd bye-substitution branches run inside the hot match loop even though the bye team index (numTeams-1) is known per round position.
perf.currentCost: For odd n, every emitted match tests `t1==numTeams-1` and `t2==numTeams-1`. Only one slot per round ever holds the phantom team, so most of these branches are wasted work in the inner loop.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist the odd-n handling: the phantom team (index numTeams-1) only ever appears as t2 of slot i==0 or rotates predictably; compute which single slot contains it per round and patch that one match to -1 after the inner loop, leaving the inner loop branch-free.
perf.rationale: Removes two comparisons per match from the inner loop for the odd-n case, converting them into a single post-loop fix-up. Smaller inner-loop body, better vectorization of the common emit path.
perf.risk: Must correctly identify the phantom slot each round to preserve identical -1 placement; if mis-derived, byes land on wrong matches. Low impact and only benefits odd n; verify slot mapping against current output before applying.

perf.summary: Inner loop recomputes (r+c)%n and a multiply r*n per cell; replace modulo with a running counter and strength-reduce the row base.
perf.currentCost: Each of n^2 cells does `grid[r*n+c] = (r+c)%n + 1` — a multiply (r*n) recomputable as a running base, and a remainder per cell. n^2 remainders dominate for large n and are not vectorizable.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist row base: `int* row = grid + r*n;` (or maintain `int baseIdx` incremented by n each row). For the value, maintain `int v = (r % n); for(c...){ row[c] = v + 1; v++; if(v==n) v=0; }`. This removes the per-cell modulo (replaced by compare+reset) and the per-cell multiply.
perf.rationale: (r+c)%n increases by 1 each step and wraps at n, so a running counter with a single compare/reset reproduces it exactly while eliminating n^2 integer remainders and n^2 multiplies. The resulting loop is a simple increment Burst can pipeline well.
perf.risk: None semantically: v starts at r%n and steps identically to (r+c)%n, wrapping at n; +1 offset preserved. n>=1 assumed (n==0 writes nothing, same as original). Pure strength reduction.
